g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the reward (priority routing for 60 minutes) before the ad and the user can ignore it. Declining changes nothing, and the 'if the ad fails' field covers both no game available and an unverified play.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of priority routing (queue_priority), which has no cash value.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event: returning from the Upgrade entry without subscribing, then opening a chat from My Chats. It does not use anything the user typed.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The idea adds an optional temporary boost and removes or caps nothing free. Normal speed is unchanged when the user declines.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement field puts the offer inside the conversation, as the character's own words at the end of its reply. That is an offer sent as a message and dressed up as chat content, which the gate forbids.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Priority routing is sold in Janitor+ (l02, s02.e06), and m03 infers a normal-priority queue for free users from s02.e07. The app therefore charges for the resource the reward gives.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about the app are supported: Janitor+ sells priority routing (s02.e06), the profile menu has a permanent Upgrade entry (s09.e31), and My Chats exists (s06). The cost claim and the new note and copy are proposal content or predictions, not claims about the app today.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The subscribers field says subscribers already have priority routing and never see the offer line, so payers are not asked to play.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward lasts 60 minutes and ends, with a cap of 2 per day. It is a time-limited sample of one benefit, not lasting access or the plan's main benefit, and it takes nothing from other users.

c5_moment.reason: The offer comes at the end of a character reply, which is a finished action, and only after the user has looked at the paid plan. It does not interrupt a task in progress.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The unit is a play-to-earn sponsored game, and the reward is granted after the play (flow step 4). The trigger, returning from the Upgrade entry and opening a chat, is an app event the app can detect.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names Janitor+ priority routing, the profile menu's Upgrade entry (s09.e31) and My Chats, so it is specific to this app.

other_concern: Chat behavior and the free-tier queue were never observed (the open question says the chat probe is needed). The 'hour of priority' cost claim is unverified. Detecting 'came back without subscribing' needs reliable state tracking.
